newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude - Steady, Oman traded at firmer levels.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - Steady, Oman traded at firmer levels.

text.p: Confirmation of lower export volumes from Indonesia for September kept Asian crude prices steady on Monday, traders said.
But activity on the market was mainly centred around the Middle East crude trading for October, they added.
The Middle East market was holding its strength, following the first October Oman trade done at MPM +3 cents per barrel on Friday.
A second Oman cargo for October was traded between European majors, at MPM +5 cents.
"It's not a runaway market, but prices are quite firm" said a trader with a major oil company.
October Qatar Marine was widely heard sold by a major at QGPC +8 cents, but could not be confirmed.
Further support for the October market was seen with the last September Abu Dhabi and Masila cargoes finally finding homes, at relatively strong prices.
A Japanese refiner bought two 750,000 barrel cargoes of September Lower Zakum from two European majors at 8 cents per barrel over the official ADNOC price.
The same buyer also bought 500,000 barrels of September Umm Shaif at ADNOC +8 cents from one of the European majors.
Earlier September Lower Zakum and Umm Shaif cargoes were traded only at premiums of 2 cents and 6 cents respectively.
Traders were uncertain why the refiner decided to buy the September cargoes, with some speculating a lack of Iraqi crudes as the reason.
But others said that the refiner may have bought September cargoes expecting prices to be even stronger in October.
Far East crude trading remained limited, apart from a Minas sale done last week at ICP +35 cents from an equity producer to a U.S. major.
September Minas barrels were offered around ICP +50/60, with sellers citing reduced export allocations of Indonesian heavy crudes as the reason for higher levels.
In its September allocations which were released earlier on Monday, Indonesia increased heavy Minas export volumes slightly, but sharply cut heavy Widuri and Cinta exports.
This was to meet increased domestic demand following the full startup of the new 60,000 bpd crude distillation unit at Balikpapan.
Minas allocations were up 11,000 bpd to to 49,000 bpd.
But the September volumes of Cinta and Widuri were reduced by 74 percent from August to just 21,000 bpd.
